title: Reach, fidelity, costs and utilities of a nurse-led heart failure clinic in a regional hospital: a hybrid implementation study
abstract: Aim: to measure the delivery and cost of a nurse-led heart failure clinic and collect the inputs a later economic evaluation needs. Design: 12-month hybrid implementation-effectiveness study with a concurrent comparison of 90-day outcomes against two hospitals without a clinic. Results will be written after the study.
introduction: The finance committee asked for a cost per QALY, but no usable effect estimate exists for a nurse-led regional clinic, and a recorded search returned no records. The region needs measured delivery, costs and utilities before any credible valuation.
methods: A RE-AIM structure guides measurement of reach and fidelity from a short visit form. Utilities are collected at the first visit and at three months, clinic time is costed by activity, and 90-day outcomes are compared with two hospitals without a clinic after data office approval.
results: No data have been collected yet. The report will present reach and fidelity by month, cost per episode, paired utility change and, if linkage is approved, the adjusted 90-day comparison.
discussion: The discussion will state what the measured delivery and costs imply for extending the clinic. It will list what a later economic evaluation still needs.
limitations: The comparison between hospitals is non-randomised, and utilities are measured only in clinic patients. The study covers one clinic for 12 months.
conclusion: To be written after the study. It will not report a cost per QALY.
